one_line: Structured customer-agent recovery handoff for failed cloud-hosted checkout flows.
what_it_does: Embeds an origin-bound WebMCP runtime that lets a customer agent inspect a simulated incident, apply an approved recovery, preserve the cart, and verify checkout.
leverage_rationale: The page exposes private diagnostics and constrained recovery as a state-tied handoff; general UI driving would be less reliable and cannot safely access the same structured incident contract.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies one purpose-built WebMCP support handoff tied to current checkout state.
Recovery is constrained, verified, and escalates on unsupported or failed cases.
Agent does not place the order and host token is not shipped to the browser runtime.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent simulated end-to-end checkout recovery, and frame sheets show a Host Whisperer interface progressing to a product page, but no transcript or direct tool log is provided.
execution_evidence: Demo is described as repeatable in-browser with simulated hosting failure.
Frame sheets show repeated interactive states and a final Geralt XL product interface.
No transcript and no legible WebMCP call are visible.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete, costly customer-support failure mode while preserving customer intent and preventing unsafe order placement.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets checkout errors that leave customers unsure whether to refresh, wait, or contact support.
Cart preservation, private diagnostics, verification, and escalation are explicitly designed around the failure case.
creativity_rationale: The customer-agent recovery handoff is a fresh application of WebMCP to operational support, with meaningful authority boundaries rather than a generic chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Website state, developer-approved recovery, and customer intent are deliberately split across parties.
Downloaded origin-bound plugin and one purpose-built handoff are distinctive implementation choices.
usability_note: Simple customer-facing progress and preserved cart are strong; setup is aimed at developers.
red_flags: No explicit tool-call transcript; visual evidence is indirect.
standouts: Private diagnostics plus approved recovery and independent checkout verification.
Escalates rather than pretending unsupported recovery succeeded.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific support concept with credible safety boundaries and a coherent claimed workflow.

one_line: Human-approved coordination of community-event needs and shared resources.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect needs and resources, stage a compatible assignment plan, and surface it to an organizer for approval before commit and repair.
leverage_rationale: Stable IDs, schemas, shared live state, structured errors, and approval-gated writes materially outperform UI inference for constrained resource coordination.
leverage_evidence: Nine tools share a CoordinationStore with the human interface.
Agent can stage but cannot approve; premature commit returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
Van unavailability is detected and one assignment repaired while seven remain.
execution_rationale: The fixed scenario is unusually well specified and includes proposal, failed authorization, approval, commit, intentional breakage, and partial repair; visual frames corroborate dashboards and approval/tool states.
execution_evidence: Seven needs and fifteen resources are specified.
Frames show proposal CM-F0E8CD, 100% projected coverage, assignment metrics, WebMCP tool dialogs, and plan review.
Human approval boundary and activity trail are described and visually suggested.
impact_rationale: Community organizers have a real coordination problem involving capacity, distance, requirements, and consequential commitments; the product directly supports it.
impact_evidence: Saturday Community Day scenario tracks concrete chairs, driver, meals, and other needs.
Organizer retains approval of exact assignments and can review exceptions.
creativity_rationale: The explicit division between agent optimization and human commitment, plus deliberate fault repair, is a strong and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: No approval/reset/availability tools are exposed, preserving human authority.
Repair demonstrates selective recovery rather than hiding a broken plan.
usability_note: Shared proposal state, metrics, activity trail, and review UI support organizer comprehension.
red_flags: Scenario is fixed/demo data rather than broad deployment evidence.
standouts: Fault injection and one-for-one repair while preserving valid assignments.
advance_reason: Excellent evidence-backed human-agent coordination workflow with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Human-governed proposal, authorization, execution, and verification control layer.
what_it_does: Allows an agent to inspect policy and propose a $25 refund, while humans separately approve and execute it and an independent readback verifies the observed result.
leverage_rationale: Structured proposal, audit, policy, and verification surfaces encode authority separation and fail-closed checks that generic UI automation cannot reliably guarantee.
leverage_evidence: Seven safe WebMCP tools cover inspection, policy, proposal, audit, and verification support.
Agent cannot approve or execute; post-approval substitution, duplicates, and mismatched evidence fail closed.
Independent readback marks the exact $25 result VERIFIED.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a complete consequential-action lifecycle and six gallery images provide packaging/UI evidence, though there is no video transcript or submitted video.
execution_evidence: Explicit starting state, proposal, human approval, separate execution, and verification are described.
Gallery evidence is present; frame-sheet review was rate-limited and did not provide additional readable detail.
impact_rationale: Consequential business actions such as refunds need exactly this separation of assistance from authority and proof.
impact_evidence: Concrete order/refund scenario within a stated $30 policy limit.
Addresses money, access, records, and operational-state risks described in the submission.
creativity_rationale: It makes the negative capability—what an AI must not do—the central interaction model, with independent verification as a first-class step.
creativity_evidence: Proposal, authorization, execution, and proof are deliberately separate.
Fail-closed boundary tests are part of the concept, not merely implementation detail.
usability_note: Clear governance stages are valuable, though added review/execution steps increase friction.
red_flags: No direct video/tool-call evidence in packet.
advance_reason: Strong governance concept with a concrete, coherent consequential-action lifecycle.

one_line: Typed browser-agent queries for heterogeneous game servers with shared human-visible results.
what_it_does: Provides discovery and bounded server-query tools, routes them through the same API as the form, and renders provenance, warnings, and raw JSON for inspection.
leverage_rationale: Typed canonical game profiles and bounded inputs reduce protocol inference and errors, but a competent agent could achieve much of the same through the form with friction.
leverage_evidence: Two document-scoped tools expose canonical profiles and bounded query parameters.
Shared route and shared UI preserve result semantics and handoff.
Validation, throttling, cancellation, warnings, and raw results are surfaced.
execution_rationale: The product scope and shared query path are coherent and the demo is alive, but no video or frame sheets visibly prove an agent invocation or returned query.
execution_evidence: Six game profiles and a documented query flow are specified.
No submitted video; screenshot is packaging only.
impact_rationale: Players, server admins, and support users have a concrete need for quickly checking heterogeneous game-server status without protocol knowledge.
impact_evidence: Handles different protocols, ports, modes, response shapes, and human inspection needs.
Result provenance and warnings improve practical troubleshooting.
creativity_rationale: A useful synthesis of typed agent tools and a game-server playground, but the underlying query utility is a familiar category.
creativity_evidence: Agent-to-human handoff with populated controls and raw evidence is a thoughtful angle.
usability_note: Canonical profiles and populated controls reduce expertise required for both agents and people.
red_flags: No video frame sheets were substantively available as readable evidence.
Live external server behavior is not demonstrated in packet visuals.
standouts: Shared agent/person result surface with provenance and raw JSON.
advance_reason: Useful and credible concept, but packet lacks end-to-end execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: Browser-based front-end editor whose agent can build and audit accessible sites in one tab.
what_it_does: Combines multi-file code editing, live preview, WCAG auditing, responsive preview, design-token checks, and WebMCP agent access.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects the coding agent to live editor, preview, and accessibility audit state, closing a multi-tool handoff that otherwise requires brittle browser driving.
leverage_evidence: Editor exposes code, preview, audit, and agent against the same current artifact.
Every preview refresh runs WCAG checks and reports exact elements/fixes.
Design tokens and compatibility checks are integrated into the agent-visible loop.
execution_rationale: The claimed product scope is ambitious and coherent, but the submitted video is a Rick Astley music video rather than product evidence and no readable frame evidence is available; execution must be capped.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text details a substantial editor/audit workflow.
FACTS identify a 213-second unrelated video title and no transcript.
No usable product-motion evidence is established.
impact_rationale: Front-end teams have a real recurring problem of accessibility and design-system regressions across disconnected tools; an integrated audit loop could materially help.
impact_evidence: Targets accessibility omissions and CSS token drift during AI-assisted development.
Reports WCAG impact, plain-English fixes, and exact elements.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-native coding, live preview, automated a11y, multi-device checks, and design-token enforcement is an ambitious and fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Accessibility is positioned as part of the build loop rather than a post hoc checker.
DESIGN.md is treated as source of truth for AI-written CSS.
usability_note: Single-tab workflow is compelling, though broad feature scope may increase complexity.
red_flags: Submitted video title is unrelated music content, so visual execution claims cannot be checked.
Very broad scope with thin packet verification.
standouts: Design-token and browser-baseline checks integrated into editor.
advance_reason: Promising concept but the required product evidence is missing/invalid, sharply limiting claimed execution.

one_line: A shared decision room where one browser AI supplies six named perspectives for human review.
what_it_does: Maintains a live brief, agenda, evidence-linked contributions, recommendations, revision state, and visible human approval/rejection workflow.
leverage_rationale: Stateful typed tools let the agent read and update a shared decision record with revision-safe mutations; this is materially better than a detached chat transcript.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools cover session, context, agenda, perspectives, contributions, recommendation, and decision record.
expectedRevision and operationId support concurrency and safe retries.
Human approves/rejects/requests revision in the visible form.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and specific, including budget revision invalidating an earlier recommendation, but no video is supplied and frame evidence is not readable enough to verify end-to-end behavior.
execution_evidence: Concrete R20,000 to R8,000 revision scenario is described.
One browser AI and human-controlled review are clearly scoped.
No video; screenshot/frames provide only partial packaging/workflow evidence.
impact_rationale: Founders and teams genuinely need structured decision support under changing constraints, and preserving alternatives/reservations can improve review quality.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and consequential launch-budget scenario.
Evidence-linked contributions and stale-recommendation handling address real decision friction.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate use of one agent adopting named perspectives, with a durable review record and revision semantics, is a memorable alternative to multi-agent theater.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly does not run six independent workers or call a model API.
Stateful collaboration and human decision boundary are central.
usability_note: Visible alternatives and reservations help review; six perspectives may create cognitive load.
red_flags: No submitted video and no direct tool transcript.
Perspectives are role prompts on one browser AI, not independent experts.
standouts: Human-controlled review channel with evidence-linked contributions.
advance_reason: Strong interaction model and meaningful shared-state leverage despite limited visual execution proof.

what_it_does: Lets an agent add and weight entries, draw one or multiple winners, rename results, manage exclusions, and mutate the same state a person sees.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools make repeated draws and state mutations convenient and precise, but a general agent can drive this simple UI comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Tools mirror straightforward UI actions such as add, draw, update, reset, and multi-draw.
Shared underlying state is claimed, but the task is simple and no meaningful capability is unique to WebMCP.
execution_rationale: The described demo is a complete small workflow, but there are no video frame sheets and only packaging/gallery evidence, so end-to-end completion is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Eight planets, weighted entries, single draw, rename, reset, and three-winner draw are specified.
No submitted video frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Random draws serve games, classrooms, giveaways, and lightweight decisions, but the packet establishes only a generic small utility audience.
impact_evidence: Supports weighted entries, exclusions, and multiple winners.
No specific high-value audience or distinctive need is demonstrated.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native framing and direct state access are a modest new angle on a familiar randomizer.
creativity_evidence: Same application state is operated by person and agent.
Planet demo gives the utility a playful example but not a novel concept.
usability_note: Simple operations and shared state should be easy to understand.
red_flags: WebMCP appears primarily a convenience layer for basic CRUD/randomization.
standouts: Clear agent-native state mutation demo concept.
advance_reason: Functional-looking but low WebMCP delta and modest originality/impact.

one_line: Progress-gated Terraria companion that only exposes advice for the player's unlocked stage.
what_it_does: Tracks defeated bosses and inventory, then exposes stage-appropriate crafting, housing, and next-step guidance through dynamically gated WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic tool registration makes game progression an actual capability boundary, reducing spoiler and hallucination risk in a way generic page driving cannot reliably enforce.
leverage_evidence: Eight tools are always on and three appear only at the player's stage.
Later-stage tools are intentionally not registered.
Game data and gating live in the page and are shared with demo scenarios.
execution_rationale: The concept and staged tool design are coherent, but the author explicitly says filming used fake scenarios and a stand-in screenshot; no video is submitted, limiting observed execution.
execution_evidence: Vite/React/TypeScript static demo with eleven tools is described.
Author acknowledges fake scenarios/stand-in screenshot for filming.
No submitted video; gallery/screenshot packaging only.
impact_rationale: Progress-sensitive help addresses a real player desire for useful guidance without spoilers or invented recipes, especially for progression games.
impact_evidence: Motivating problem is explicit: wiki spoilers and chat hallucinations.
Crafting, housing, and next-step assistance are directly tied to unlocked progress.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP tool availability itself as a spoiler firewall is a notably original interaction and capability-gating model.
creativity_evidence: Stage changes dynamically alter the agent's available tools.
The product intentionally limits knowledge rather than merely prompting the model.
usability_note: Second-monitor companion and scenario setup are approachable; browser compatibility caveat remains.
red_flags: Fake demo scenarios and stand-in screenshot admitted.
Model may still recall game content outside exposed tools.
standouts: Tool registration as progression-aware spoiler control.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value game companion concept with meaningful WebMCP capability gating.

one_line: Local-file WebMCP cartridges that give agents safe in-tab media, OCR, and SQLite operations.
what_it_does: Loads WASM-backed tool collections for local files so agents can inspect media, OCR scans, trim video, and query SQLite without uploads, servers, or installation.
leverage_rationale: The product's core capability—letting a browser agent operate on private local files through dynamically loaded structured tools without upload or local MCP setup—is impractical to replicate comparably with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: 22 tools operate on local file handles in-tab; bytes are not exposed to the agent.
Cartridges dynamically add/remove capabilities through WebMCP.
WASM ffmpeg, tesseract, and sqlite provide local operations with declared read-only/consequential annotations.
execution_rationale: The 94-second product video has a transcript describing a concrete inspect-find-trim-OCR flow, and packet text includes cancellation and refused-delete states; strong claimed end-to-end evidence.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes loading media, probing, sampling frames, OCR, and trimming real files.
No upload/server/install is central to the demonstrated workflow.
Activity rail shows cancelled transcode and refused DELETE according to packet text.
impact_rationale: Privacy-preserving local file operations solve a clear gap for creators, analysts, and ordinary users who need agent help without uploading sensitive media or installing an unaudited server.
impact_evidence: Concrete video/OCR/SQLite use cases are identified.
Files stay in the tab and no API key, account, server, or upload is required.
creativity_rationale: The cartridge abstraction and zero-setup, WASM-powered local agent hands are a highly original and ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: A cartridge is a URL-level unit between one tool and every tool on a page.
Combines dynamic tool collections, local WASM capabilities, safety annotations, and untrusted OCR handling.
usability_note: Drop-file workflow and no setup are excellent; broad tool surface may require careful affordances.
red_flags: WASM performance and browser compatibility may constrain real-world files.
Consequential local operations still require careful user oversight.
standouts: Dynamic cartridge tool collections with safe handle-based security model.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and originality, backed by direct product video evidence and a compelling privacy benefit.

one_line: Shared travel workspace for agent-assisted destination research and itinerary building.
what_it_does: Lets people and agents search destinations, compare travel options, inspect details, and assemble a visible itinerary while keeping decisions human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured itinerary state and agent/person handoff improve reliability over copying between sites, but much of the outcome remains achievable through ordinary browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Search, compare, inspect, and itinerary operations are exposed in one shared workspace.
Focused destination navigation and visible human-controlled itinerary state are described.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a plausible travel workspace, but no video frame sheets are submitted and the supplied prompt ends before the full about text, limiting evidence.
execution_evidence: Three gallery images and a Devpost screenshot are listed.
No submitted video or transcript.
No end-to-end agent result is visibly established in available packet evidence.
impact_rationale: Travel planning is a real, broad coordination problem involving fragmented search and itinerary information, and a shared workspace can reduce copying friction.
impact_evidence: Explicitly targets fragmented search, hotel, map, booking, and notes workflows.
Human-controlled planning is a credible user need.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent travel workspace is a competent synthesis with a useful handoff model, but travel planners are an established category.
creativity_evidence: Destination-focused progressive disclosure and shared itinerary state are the clearest new angles.
usability_note: Focused destination view may reduce overload; breadth of travel data could complicate consistency.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or transcript.
Packet about text is incomplete in the supplied prompt.
standouts: Shared itinerary state with human control.
advance_reason: Clear use case, but insufficient execution and agent-interaction evidence compared with stronger packets.
